title: McLaren’s New Logo Throws Back For The Future

body_markdown:
British supercar maker and race team McLaren has a new brand identity that takes inspiration from Bruce McLaren’s family roots.


The new logo already adorns the company website and will soon start to appear on road and race cars. The wordmark is based on the sign above Les and Ruth McLaren’s gas station in Remuera, New Zealand, where Bruce McLaren built his first race car,


McLaren


“Recrafting that identity for today, it reconnects McLaren with its origins while giving the brand a confident visual language for the future,” says McLaren.


While not quite as controversial as[Jaguar’s rebranding](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/the-reinvention-of-jaguar-needs-a-miracle-to-succeed/) , the new design hasn’t met with universal approval, with some commenters likening it to the Marriot Bonvoy mark, and others suggesting it’s interchangeable with any number of luxury brands.


Marriott Bonvoy


McLaren


“Throughout our history, we’ve never been content to follow established paths,” adds Chief Creative Officer, David Woodhouse. “We’ve always looked ahead, driven by a restless desire to innovate, create and push beyond expectations. This evolution of our visual identity captures that spirit. It’s a reflection of the journey we are on as a company. It marks the beginning of a new chapter for McLaren, giving a physical expression to the ambition, creativity and forward momentum that is shaping our future.”


That future has recently been bolstered with a £500 M ($666 M) investment that will see McLaren add a second factory and expand its road car portfolio into the SUV market. McLaren’s machine is expected to be challenger to the Lamborghini Urus and[Aston Martin DBX](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-2026-aston-martin-dbx-s-adds-aggression-and-loses-weight/) rather than a rival for the[Ferrari Purosangue](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ferrari-purosangue-adds-poise-with-handling-pack/) .


Meanwhile, the first chance to see the new McLaren mark in the real world will be at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on September 24-26. The first road car to wear the new wording across its rear will be the limited-run[McL 6GT](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-mcl-6gt-does-something-mclaren-never-does-look-backwards/) (top).
